name: Things That Go Bump
blurb: Glimmer Falls was built on top of a lot of yesterdays, and on Halloween week they all want to say hello. Porch lights blink, buses that stopped running in 1958 make one more stop, and the junkyard forgets how to end.

encounters.title: The Endless Lot
encounters.place: Rusty's Junkyard, somewhere past midnight
encounters.text: You blink on your own front lawn and open your eyes between two rusted station wagons. This is Rusty's Junkyard, except the rows of cars never end. Every car is the same wood-paneled wagon, every radio is on, and every radio is playing the same slow-dance ballad from the 1959 prom, "Moonlight on the Quarry," one beat out of sync, forever.
encounters.art: A teenager in pajamas standing in an endless junkyard aisle of identical rusted wood-paneled station wagons stretching to the horizon in straight rows under a full moon, every dashboard radio glowing the same amber, low mist drifting between the rows, the teen's bare feet in the dirt, cold blue moonlight and warm amber dash lights, wide shot down the rows

choices.label: Follow the song to wherever it is loudest

success.text: The ballad swells, row after row, until you reach the car crusher. Its radio is the only one playing the song on the right beat. You click it off. Silence rolls outward like a wave, the rows fold away like a deck of cards, and you are standing at the junkyard gate with the stars where they belong.
success.art: A teenager reaching into the cab of a car crusher to switch off a glowing radio, rows of identical station wagons folding away behind them like playing cards, the junkyard gate ahead under starlight

failure.text: The song gets louder, then closer, then inside your head. The nearest radio dial glows like a cat's eye and the needle swings toward you. You lean in to turn it off and the static grabs you by the collar and pulls you straight through the speaker grille. The night is not done with you yet.
failure.art: A teenager being pulled face-first into the glowing speaker grille of a station wagon dashboard radio, streams of amber static wrapping around them, endless identical cars behind

choices.label: Hotwire a wagon and drive straight through the rows

success.text: Two wires, one spark, and the engine coughs awake. You floor it down the aisle and the identical cars peel aside like curtains. The radio finally changes stations on its own, to KGLM, and you roll to a stop in your own driveway with the headlights off and the engine still ticking.
success.art: A wood-paneled station wagon bursting out of a misty junkyard maze with headlights blazing, rows of identical cars parting like curtains, a suburban driveway glowing ahead

failure.text: The engine catches, the wheel turns itself, and the wagon drives you in a slow, polite circle around the same three rows while the ballad plays on. You wake in its back seat at dawn with a seatbelt buckled across you that you never fastened.
failure.art: A teenager asleep in the back seat of a station wagon at dawn, a seatbelt buckled over them, the steering wheel turning by itself, a junkyard misty and gray outside

choices.label: Scratch an X on every car you pass

success.text: On the fortieth car you find your own X already waiting. It is a loop. So you look for the one car without a mark, the one that smells like motor oil instead of old perfume. Its back door opens onto the junkyard office, and there is a coffee can of loose change under the seat.
success.art: A teenager pointing at a single unmarked station wagon among dozens scratched with X marks, its back door open onto a lit junkyard office, a coffee can of coins on the seat

failure.text: Every car you reach already has an X on it. Hundreds of them, then thousands, all scratched in your handwriting, some of them rusted over as if you made them years ago. You stop scratching. The radios keep playing.
failure.art: An endless row of identical station wagons each scratched with the same X, some old and rusted, a teenager staring at their own key in their hand

encounters.title: Yes, No, Goodbye
encounters.place: A wood-paneled basement rec room on Crystal Street
encounters.text: Somebody brought a Spirit-Talk board from the Starlight Mall toy store, and the slumber party has been giggling over it for an hour. Then the planchette moves before anyone touches it. It spells your name. Then it spells OPEN THE DOOR, and the door to the garage starts to rattle in its frame.
encounters.art: A wood-paneled basement rec room at night, five teens in sleeping bags on shag carpet around a store-bought talking board, the heart-shaped planchette sliding across it with every hand pulled back, a lava lamp glowing red on a shelf, the door to the garage rattling in its frame in the background, one teen pointing at the door, red lava light and flashlight glow, medium wide shot

choices.label: Ask the spirit, politely, who it is

success.text: P-A-T-T-Y. She was twelve. Her own slumber party got rained out in 1960 and she has been waiting ever since. You let her play one round of light-as-a-feather, and everyone swears their fingers lifted. The planchette glides to GOODBYE, and the garage door goes still.
success.art: Teens in a circle doing light as a feather in a candlelit basement, a faint glowing girl in a 1960 nightgown laughing among them, the talking board planchette resting on goodbye

failure.text: The planchette spins like a top, flies across the room and sticks in the wood paneling. Every sleeping bag zips itself shut, with people still in them. When you get them unzipped, there is a cold print of a small hand on your wrist that will not warm up until morning.
failure.art: A plastic planchette stuck in wood paneling, sleeping bags zipped shut and squirming on a basement floor, a frosty small handprint glowing on a teenager's wrist

choices.label: Slam the planchette onto GOODBYE

success.text: You slap the planchette down on GOODBYE so hard the board bends. The lights snap on, the furnace kicks in, and the garage door is just a garage door again. The board is cardboard and a price sticker. Somebody laughs, and then everybody does.
success.art: A teenager slamming a hand down on a talking board's goodbye with the overhead lights flaring on in a basement rec room, friends startled then laughing

failure.text: The planchette pushes back with the strength of a grown-up. It drags your hand across the letters, H-E-R-E, and the garage door bangs open on an empty, dark garage where the bicycles are all spinning their wheels.
failure.art: A dark open garage with every bicycle's wheels spinning by themselves, a teenager's hand dragged across a talking board in the foreground

encounters.title: Porch Light Code
encounters.place: Crystal Street, two in the morning
encounters.text: You wake up because your room keeps flashing. Outside, every porch light on the cul-de-sac is blinking in perfect unison: long, short, short, long. No one is awake. No one is on the porches. The pattern stops, starts over, and waits, like somebody repeating a question.
encounters.art: A suburban cul-de-sac at two in the morning seen from the street, every porch light on every house blinking in unison, every porch empty, the roundabout garden dark in the middle with a faint purple glow, a teenager in pajamas silhouetted in an upstairs bedroom window with a hand on the glass, blue night and flashing yellow porch lights, wide shot

choices.label: Write the blinks down and decode them

success.text: Dots and dashes fill your notebook. L-O-O-K U-N-D-E-R M-A-T. Under your own doormat is a 1944 silver half-dollar and a note in faded pencil: Thank you for noticing us. Every porch light gives one warm, long blink and goes out for the night.
success.art: A teenager kneeling at a front door holding a silver half-dollar and a faded pencil note found under the doormat, porch lights along the street glowing warm gold

failure.text: You get as far as R-U-N before every porch light goes dark at once. Then one light comes back on. It is not on a porch. It is your bedside lamp, behind you, and you did not leave it on.
failure.art: A dark cul-de-sac with every porch light out, a single bedside lamp glowing in a teenager's bedroom behind them as they stare out the window

choices.label: Flash your own light back and answer

success.text: You blink back H-I. The street goes still. Then, one by one, the porch lights spell H-I back, slow and happy, like old neighbors waving from across the years. A dog howls somewhere, cheerful, and the lights settle into a soft, ordinary glow.
success.art: A teenager on a lawn aiming a flashlight at a row of porch lights that glow warm and friendly in reply, ghostly outlines of 1950s neighbors waving from the porches

failure.text: Your flashlight bulb pops with a sound like a cap gun. Every porch light on the street swivels on its bracket to point at you, and they stay pointed until sunrise, warm on the back of your neck no matter where you stand.
failure.art: Porch light fixtures on every house twisted on their brackets to aim at one teenager on a dark lawn holding a dead flashlight

encounters.title: Candles at Pinecrest
encounters.place: Pinecrest Cemetery, after the gates are locked
encounters.text: A line of people in old-fashioned clothes is walking between the headstones, each one carrying a candle that does not flicker in the wind. Bonnets, fedoras, a girl in a poodle skirt. The last one in line turns, smiles, and holds out a spare candle to you.
encounters.art: A silent procession of pale translucent figures in clothes from many decades walking single file between moonlit headstones, a woman in a bonnet, a man in a fedora, a girl in a poodle skirt, each holding a candle whose flame stands perfectly still in the wind, the last figure turning to offer a spare candle to a teenager crouched behind a stone mausoleum, cold moonlight and warm candle glow, wide shot

choices.label: Take the candle and walk with them

success.text: You walk with them to the cemetery gate. They are the town's forgotten dead, heading out for the one Halloween they never got. At the gate they each say their name to you, and you say yours back. The candle stays lit in your hand all the way home and never melts.
success.art: A teenager walking at the end of a ghostly candlelit procession through an open cemetery gate, the figures turning to say their names, warm candlelight on the teen's face

failure.text: The candle gets heavier with every step until it weighs as much as a brick. The procession files into a mausoleum and the iron door swings shut with you inside. The groundskeeper lets you out at dawn and does not ask a single question.
failure.art: A teenager pressed against the bars of a mausoleum door at dawn, an extinguished candle at their feet, a groundskeeper with a ring of keys approaching

choices.label: Duck behind a headstone and count them

success.text: You count forty-eight. The forty-eighth stops, tips his fedora in your direction, and keeps walking. You were seen, and you were let be. On the headstone you hid behind, someone has left a tarnished subway token and a peppermint.
success.art: A ghostly man in a fedora tipping his hat toward a headstone where a teenager hides, a tarnished token and a peppermint resting on the stone

failure.text: Forty-eight. Forty-nine. Fifty. There is one more every time you start over. When you finally reach the end of the line, the last candle is not in front of you. Its warmth is on the back of your neck.
failure.art: A teenager crouched behind a headstone counting on their fingers, a candle glowing directly behind their head held by a pale hand

encounters.title: The Last Bus
encounters.place: Corner of Crystal Street and Quarry Road, three a.m.
encounters.text: A round-nosed yellow school bus from the fifties idles at the corner where no bus has stopped in decades. The sign says GLIMMER FALLS ELEMENTARY: FIELD TRIP. The doors fold open with a sigh. Inside, a busload of kids in saddle shoes and cardigans press their faces to the windows and wave at you.
encounters.art: A round-nosed 1950s yellow school bus idling at a foggy suburban street corner at three in the morning, its folding doors open, translucent kids in saddle shoes and cardigans pressing their faces to every window and waving, the driver's face hidden under a cap, a teenager on the curb in a hooded sweatshirt, headlights glowing in the fog, wide shot

choices.label: Climb aboard and ask where the field trip goes

success.text: The kids scoot over to make room. The field trip goes everywhere: the old drive-in, the soda fountain, the quarry beach before it was drained. They sing the whole way. At dawn the bus drops you at your door and a girl hands you a felt pennant that reads I WENT.
success.art: A teenager riding a glowing 1950s school bus full of singing ghost kids past a vintage drive-in theater, a felt pennant being handed over the seat

failure.text: The doors close and the bus drives you all over town. Every stop is your house, but wrong: painted a different color, a different car in the driveway, a different family in the window. It lets you off at sunrise in your pajamas, three blocks from home.
failure.art: A teenager in pajamas stepping off a ghostly school bus at sunrise onto an unfamiliar version of their own street, a house painted the wrong color

choices.label: Wave back and keep your feet on the curb

success.text: You wave with your whole arm. The kids light up and wave harder. The doors fold shut, the bus pulls away, and its taillights break apart into a swarm of fireflies that drift up over the rooftops of Crystal Street.
success.art: A teenager waving from the curb as a ghostly school bus pulls away, its red taillights dissolving into a swarm of fireflies rising over suburban rooftops

failure.text: You raise your hand and every kid on the bus stops waving at once. They all turn to look past you, at your house, and they keep looking as the bus rolls away, until it is gone around a corner that is not there in daylight.
failure.art: A row of ghost children on a school bus all turned to stare at a single suburban house, a teenager frozen on the curb with one hand raised

encounters.title: Footsteps in the Attic
encounters.place: Your house, 1:13 a.m.
encounters.text: Somebody is pacing in the attic. Back and forth, back and forth, right above your bed, in hard-soled shoes. Your family is asleep. Then the pull-down ladder in the hallway creaks, unfolds itself step by step, and lands softly on the carpet like an invitation.
encounters.art: A dark suburban upstairs hallway at 1:13 in the morning, the pull-down attic ladder unfolding by itself step by step from an open ceiling hatch and landing softly on the carpet, a faint yellow light and the moving shadow of pacing feet visible through the hatch, a teenager in pajamas standing in their bedroom doorway, closed doors along the hall, medium shot from low in the hallway

choices.label: Climb the ladder with a flashlight in your teeth

success.text: Up in the attic, an electric train set from 1959 is running on its own, around a little papier-mache Glimmer Falls with tiny painted houses. A boy's voice whispers, "Nobody ever came up to see it." You stay and watch three full laps. The train slows, happy, and stops at the station.
success.art: A teenager in a dusty attic watching a vintage electric train circle a papier-mache model town, flashlight beam catching floating dust, a faint boy's silhouette kneeling beside the tracks

failure.text: The ladder folds up behind you with a bang and the hatch latches. In the pitch dark the pacing stops, and then starts again, right next to you. You spend the night sitting on a box of Christmas ornaments until somebody downstairs wonders why the ladder is stuck.
failure.art: A teenager hugging their knees on a box of Christmas ornaments in a pitch-black attic, the faint outline of shoes pacing beside them in a sliver of light

choices.label: Talk to the ceiling like an old roommate

success.text: "Hey. Rough night?" The pacing stops. Then two taps: yes. You talk for an hour about school and records and who you have a crush on, and the taps answer. In the morning there is a 1950s quarter on your pillow, polished bright.
success.art: A teenager lying in bed talking up at the ceiling at night, a soft glow through the plaster above, a shiny old quarter resting on the pillow beside them

failure.text: The footsteps stop. Then they start running, back and forth, faster and faster, and the attic hatch rattles in its frame like someone pounding to get out. It goes on until the sky turns gray and your alarm clock goes off.
failure.art: An attic hatch in a dark hallway rattling violently in its frame, dust raining down, a frightened teenager peeking out from their bedroom door

encounters.title: The Hitchhiker on Tower Road
encounters.place: Tower Road, halfway down the switchbacks, midnight
encounters.text: You are coasting home from the KGLM tower when a boy in a letter jacket and a slicked pompadour steps into your bike light with his thumb out. He is dripping wet on a bone-dry night. "Lucky Strike Lanes, please," he says, polite as a church usher. "League finals. The team's waiting on me." Lucky Strike Lanes burned down in 1963. He hops onto your handlebars anyway, light as a paper bag.
encounters.art: A translucent teenage boy in a damp letter jacket and a slicked pompadour perched on the handlebars of a teenager's bicycle on a foggy mountain switchback at midnight, water dripping from his jacket onto the dry road, the bike headlight cutting through the mist, a guardrail and the small lights of a valley town far below, white headlight and gray fog, medium wide shot

choices.label: Pedal him all the way to the old lot

success.text: You pedal him down the hill and across town to the weedy lot where the lanes used to be. For one breath a neon bowling pin flickers back to life above the weeds, and you hear a crowd roar for a strike. He hops off, says "Thanks, pal," and rolls a glowing ball off into the dark. The fog goes with him.
success.art: A weedy vacant lot at night where a glowing neon bowling pin flickers in midair, a translucent boy in a letter jacket rolling a ghostly ball into the dark, a teenager on a bicycle watching from the curb

failure.text: Every turn you take leads back uphill. His wet jacket drips cold down your neck, and the road keeps unrolling into more switchbacks until your legs are jelly. At dawn you are back at the KGLM gate, by yourself, with a damp handprint on each shoulder that takes all morning to dry.
failure.art: An exhausted teenager slumped over a bicycle at a radio tower gate at dawn, two damp handprints on the shoulders of their jacket, a winding mountain road below

choices.label: Ask him what happened on league night

success.text: He frowns like a word is on the tip of his tongue. Delphine, idling behind you on her motorcycle, recites the 1963 team roster from a newspaper she has read a hundred times. At his own name he smiles and simply stops being wet. Then he stops being there at all, and the fog lifts off the whole hill like a sheet off a sofa.
success.art: A translucent boy in a letter jacket smiling and fading into moonlight on a mountain road as the fog lifts away, a teenager on a bicycle beside him holding an old folded newspaper
success.alone: He frowns like a word is on the tip of his tongue. You tell him what the library microfiche says: league night, 1963, the fire, the trophy he went back inside for. At his own name he smiles and simply stops being wet. Then he stops being there at all, and the fog lifts off the whole hill like a sheet off a sofa.

failure.text: His face goes smoky at the edges. "There was a fire?" he asks, and the smell of scorched varnish rolls over you both. He climbs off the bike, walks through the guardrail and down into the pines, calling for a strike that never comes. You hear him calling until sunrise.
failure.art: A translucent boy in a letter jacket walking through a guardrail into a dark pine forest, smoke curling off his shoulders, a teenager on a bicycle staring after him on a foggy road

choices.label: Coast to the bottom and ditch him at the stoplight

success.text: At the bottom of the hill the light turns red and you swerve hard into the Quik-Stop lot. He floats right on without you, still sitting in midair where your handlebars were, all the way down Main Street, waving cheerfully. The night cashier, who saw everything, slides you a free cocoa and the change from the tip jar.
success.art: A translucent boy in a letter jacket sitting in midair as he floats down an empty small-town main street at night, waving, a teenager on a bicycle braking hard in a convenience store parking lot

failure.text: You swerve. He does not. He just keeps sitting on your handlebars, dripping and patient, while you pedal frantic circles around the Quik-Stop lot. "Wrong way, pal," he says kindly, and the bike tugs toward a road you have never seen, lined with neon signs that went dark years ago.
failure.art: A teenager on a bicycle pedaling onto a strange dreamlike road lined with flickering old neon signs, a translucent boy in a letter jacket riding the handlebars and pointing the way

encounters.title: Dryer Number Thirteen
encounters.place: Suds-O-Mat 24-Hour Laundromat, Main Street, two a.m.
encounters.text: You are washing the slime out of your jacket at the all-night laundromat, the only customer under the buzzing lights. Dryer number thirteen starts up by itself, no quarter. Through its round window tumble clothes nobody has worn in thirty years: a poodle skirt, a Sunday hat, a tiny sailor suit. A woman in a housecoat and pink curlers is folding at the counter, and you can see the vending machine right through her.
encounters.art: A fluorescent-lit all-night laundromat at two in the morning, a row of round-windowed dryers with one window glowing and tumbling 1950s clothes, a poodle skirt, a Sunday hat and a tiny sailor suit, a translucent woman in a quilted housecoat and pink curlers folding laundry at the counter with a vending machine visible through her body, a teenager holding a slime-covered jacket, buzzing white light, medium wide shot

choices.label: Pick up a shirt and help her fold

success.text: Glory takes the sailor suit and shows you the stage-wardrobe fold, quick and crisp, and the woman watches, delighted, humming an old radio song. When the dryer stops, the clothes are only warm air and lavender. She pats your cheek with a hand like a cool breeze, and your jacket comes out of the washer cleaner than new.
success.art: A translucent woman in curlers patting a teenager's cheek at a laundromat folding counter, a neat stack of glowing 1950s clothes dissolving into lavender mist
success.alone: You fold the way somebody once taught you, corners to corners, and the woman nods approval, humming an old radio song. When the dryer stops, the clothes are only warm air and lavender. She pats your cheek with a hand like a cool breeze, and your jacket comes out of the washer cleaner than new.

failure.text: She looks at your fold and tuts. Then she takes your jacket and folds it herself, into halves, quarters, eighths, sixteenths, until it is the size of a matchbook. You spend the rest of the night sitting on the linoleum unfolding it, one stubborn crease at a time.
failure.art: A teenager sitting on a laundromat floor at night unfolding a jacket that has been folded into a tiny square, a translucent woman in curlers watching with her arms crossed

choices.label: Yank dryer thirteen open mid-cycle

success.text: The door swings open and a warm gust of every Saturday in 1955 rolls out: fabric softener, a ballgame on the radio, kids yelling in a backyard. The tumbling clothes settle into a neat pile and fade. At the bottom of the drum is a little heap of old coins, still warm from the spin.
success.art: A teenager pulling open a glowing round dryer door as warm golden mist pours out, a small heap of shining old coins at the bottom of the drum, rows of machines in a laundromat at night

failure.text: The drum keeps spinning with the door open, faster and faster, and the pull of it drags at your sleeve, your arm, your foot. You brace against the machine below and pop free, but one sneaker goes tumbling round and round in there. It is still tumbling when you hop out into the night.
failure.art: A single sneaker tumbling around inside a glowing laundromat dryer, a teenager in one sock bracing against the machines with both hands

choices.label: Feed it a quarter of your own and let her finish

success.text: You drop in a quarter, as if to say this load is on you. The cycle buzzes done, the clothes fold themselves in midair and drift into her basket, and she tips her head to you, settles the basket on her hip and walks out the door into the Main Street fog, finished at last.
success.art: A translucent woman in a housecoat carrying a basket of floating folded clothes out the glass door of a laundromat into a foggy main street, a teenager waving goodbye

failure.text: The dryer swallows your quarter and blinks for another. And another. The coin slot glows a hungry orange. By the time you give up, your pockets are turned out and dryer thirteen is still spinning, with your own laundry somehow tumbling in there too.
failure.art: A teenager with turned-out pockets in front of a laundromat dryer whose coin slot glows hungry orange, their own clothes tumbling behind the round window

encounters.title: The Ghost Light
encounters.place: The Glitter Box Playhouse stage, long after the revue
encounters.text: Every theater leaves one bare bulb burning on the stage overnight, so the ghosts can rehearse. You came back for the scarf you left in the dressing room, and the ghost light is flickering in time to a piano with no pianist. A chorus line in 1940s sequins kicks across the boards, translucent and fabulous, and their stage manager, a woman with a clipboard and a pencil behind her ear, points straight at you. "You. Understudy. Places."
encounters.art: A single bare light bulb on a metal stand glowing in the middle of a dark small-theater stage at night, a translucent chorus line in 1940s sequined costumes kicking in unison across the boards, a ghostly stage manager with a clipboard and a pencil behind her ear pointing straight at a teenager standing in the wings holding a scarf, an upright piano playing with its keys moving by themselves, warm bulb light and blue shadow, wide shot

choices.label: Step into the line and kick like your life depends on it

success.text: Frankie, still in her headset from the late show, shoves you into the line and calls the counts from the wings. Five, six, seven, eight. You kick, you turn, you nail the finale pose, and the ghostly chorus bursts into silent applause. The stage manager makes one firm check mark on her clipboard. You walk home taller.
success.art: A teenager striking a jazz-hands finale pose in the middle of a translucent sequined chorus line on a theater stage, a single bare bulb glowing, shimmering ghostly applause in the dark seats
success.alone: You count it off under your breath, five, six, seven, eight, and kick, turn, and nail the finale pose half a beat late but with total commitment. The ghostly chorus bursts into silent applause. The stage manager makes one firm check mark on her clipboard. You walk home taller.

failure.text: You kick on the wrong count and the whole chorus line goes down like dominoes, straight through you, cold as a walk-in freezer. The stage manager sighs, crosses your name off the call sheet, and the ghost light pops, leaving you groping through the dark for the exit sign.
failure.art: A translucent chorus line toppling like dominoes through a startled teenager on a dark theater stage, a bare bulb on a stand bursting in a spray of sparks

choices.label: Climb to the light booth and steady the flickering bulb

success.text: You find the right dimmer by its masking-tape label, number six, and ease the master up gently. The bulb steadies to a warm, even glow. The ghost piano finishes its song properly for the first time in forty years, and the whole chorus line takes a deep bow toward the booth, toward you.
success.art: A teenager at an old theater light board with glowing sliders in a booth above a stage, a single bulb shining warm and steady below, a translucent chorus line bowing toward the booth

failure.text: You push the wrong slider and every light in the house slams on, then off, then on, like a thunderstorm indoors. The ghosts scatter up into the rafters, deeply offended, and for the rest of the night the piano plays the same sour note every time you take a step.
failure.art: A community theater with every stage light flashing at once like a lightning storm, translucent dancers fleeing up into the rafters, a teenager wincing at a light board

choices.label: Grab your scarf and tiptoe out along the back wall

success.text: You hug the back wall, past the fly ropes and the old flats painted like Paris. The chorus never misses a beat. In the dressing room your scarf is folded neatly on the makeup counter, with two quarters on top and a lipstick kiss on the mirror. Somebody in this building likes you.
success.art: A dressing room mirror ringed with glowing bulbs, a folded scarf on the makeup counter with two coins on top, a lipstick kiss on the glass, a teenager smiling in the doorway

failure.text: A fly rope snags your sleeve and a painted Paris backdrop crashes down in front of you with a boom. Every ghost turns. The stage manager taps her pencil on the clipboard. You run, and the piano plays a frantic chase number all the way out to the parking lot.
failure.art: A painted Paris backdrop crashing down in front of a teenager backstage in a dark theater, translucent dancers in sequins turning to stare

encounters.title: Thirteen Bells
encounters.place: The bell tower at St. Jude's, the stroke of midnight
encounters.text: The bell at St. Jude's has hung silent since its rope rotted through in 1971. Tonight it rings twelve times, and then a thirteenth, and the sound rolls across Crystal Street like a slammed door. Every dog in town starts howling. From your window you can see someone up in the belfry, a bell ringer in a wool cap, hauling on a rope made of moonlight and waving you over.
encounters.art: A stone church bell tower against a full moon at midnight, the great bronze bell swinging in the belfry, a translucent bell ringer in a wool cap hauling on a glowing white rope, suburban rooftops and howling dogs in yards below, a teenager leaning out of a bedroom window in the foreground, silver moonlight, wide shot from below

choices.label: Climb the tower and help ring the last one

success.text: One hundred and twelve stairs. The ringer hands you the glowing rope, and together you pull. The fourteenth bell is soft and round, like the last note of a lullaby, and across town the dogs settle one by one. The ringer grins, tips his cap, and sits down on a beam to finally rest.
success.art: A teenager and a translucent bell ringer in a wool cap pulling a glowing rope together in a moonlit belfry, the great bronze bell swinging gently overhead

failure.text: The stairs keep going, around and around, past the belfry and up into darkness where the sky ought to be. The thirteenth bell rings again, right beside your ear, and your teeth hum for an hour. You come down at dawn still gripping the rail with both hands.
failure.art: A teenager gripping the rail of an endless spiral staircase that winds up into darkness inside a stone bell tower, a great bell glowing somewhere far above

choices.label: Knock at the rectory and ask about the old ringer

success.text: Iggy opens the door in a band T-shirt, listens, and pulls a dusty ledger off a shelf. The ringer was Sal Moretti, who rang that bell for every wedding and funeral in town for forty years and never had it rung for himself. The two of you stand in the churchyard and say his name up at the tower. The bell gives one gentle bong and goes still.
success.art: A teenager standing in a moonlit churchyard looking up at a bell tower, an open dusty ledger in their hands, a translucent bell ringer in a wool cap tipping his cap from the belfry
success.alone: The rectory is dark, but a dusty ledger sits on the step, open to Sal Moretti, who rang that bell for every wedding and funeral in town for forty years and never had it rung for himself. You stand in the churchyard and say his name up at the tower. The bell gives one gentle bong and goes still.

failure.text: The rectory door swings open by itself onto a long hallway lined with photographs of bell ringers, every one in the same wool cap. Their eyes follow you. The bell strikes thirteen again and every photo nods along in time. You back out onto the lawn and run.
failure.art: A dim church hallway lined with old photographs of bell ringers in identical wool caps, their eyes following a teenager backing toward an open door

choices.label: Shinny up the drainpipe and muffle the clapper with your jacket

success.text: You shinny up the drainpipe, swing over the ledge and stuff your jacket into the bell's mouth. The next bong comes out as a muffled thud, and the ringer laughs so hard he lets go of the rope. The night goes hush. Your jacket smells like pigeons for a week, but the whole street sleeps.
success.art: A teenager on a belfry ledge stuffing a jacket into the clapper of a great bell, a translucent bell ringer in a wool cap doubled over laughing, moonlit rooftops below

failure.text: The bell swings just as you reach it and sweeps you off the ledge like a broom. You land in the churchyard hedge, unhurt and upside down, with the bell still tolling above you. Your jacket stays up there, flapping from the clapper like a flag, for the whole town to see at breakfast.
failure.art: A teenager upside down in a churchyard hedge at night, legs in the air, a jacket flapping like a flag from the clapper of a swinging bell in the tower above

name: The Body Count
blurb: Every October somebody in a rubber mask decides Glimmer Falls needs a sequel. Babysitters, roller rinks, pumpkin patches and empty high-school hallways: the rules are the rules, and the rules say never split up.

encounters.title: Have You Checked the Children?
encounters.place: The Delgado house on Crystal Street, 11:40 p.m.
encounters.text: You are babysitting the Delgado twins for five dollars an hour and a fridge full of Bolt Cola. The kids are asleep. The phone has rung three times. Each time it is the same slow breathing, and then a voice like a rake on gravel: "Have you checked the children?" This time it adds, "Nice socks."
encounters.art: A teenage babysitter sitting on shag carpet in a dim split-level living room at 11:40 at night, clutching a yellow wall phone with a long curly cord stretched from the kitchen, mismatched striped socks on their feet, a can of soda on the floor, a paper note on the refrigerator, and behind them the dark staircase up to the bedrooms, a single lamp, medium shot

choices.label: Go upstairs and check the children

success.text: The twins are asleep, but their window is open and there is a muddy bootprint on the sill. You slam the window, lock it, and stand guard with a lamp in one hand. Outside, a shape backs off across the lawn. The next time the phone rings, it is just a click.
success.art: A teenager slamming a child's bedroom window shut, twin kids asleep under rocket-ship blankets, a muddy bootprint on the sill and a shadowy figure retreating across a lawn outside

failure.text: The twins are fine, but the closet door is open one inch and there is something standing very still behind the coats. You drag a dresser in front of it and sit there with a lamp. When the Delgados get home at one, they find you in the hall, and the closet is empty.
failure.art: A teenager sitting in a dark hallway with a table lamp raised like a club, a dresser shoved against a closet door, parents in party clothes appearing at the top of the stairs

choices.label: Call the operator and keep the voice on the line

success.text: The operator traces it to the payphone outside the Quik-Stop on Quarry Road. You call the sheriff, then watch from the window as a cruiser's lights sweep the booth. A tall figure hangs up, drops the receiver, and walks away into the trees. It does not call again tonight.
success.art: A payphone booth outside a convenience store at night lit by a sheriff cruiser's red and blue lights, a tall masked figure walking away into the trees, the receiver dangling

failure.text: "Honey," the operator says, after a long pause, "that line was disconnected in 1971." On the other end, very close to the mouthpiece, the breathing turns into a slow, delighted laugh.
failure.art: A teenager pale with fear holding a phone receiver away from their ear, a disconnected-line notice taped to an old phone on the kitchen wall

choices.label: Bundle the twins out the back to the one porch light still on

success.text: You carry one twin and drag the other in a sleeping bag across three back lawns to the only porch light on the street. Mrs. Washington is already up, rocking, a shotgun full of rock salt across her knees. "Sit," she says, and nothing follows you. She sends you home with a coffee can of salt.
success.art: A teenager hauling two sleepy kids across dark backyards toward a glowing porch where an elderly woman rocks with a rock-salt shotgun across her knees

failure.text: The back door will not open. Something in the yard knocks on the glass, three slow knocks. You hustle the twins into the bathtub with every pillow in the house and sing them commercial jingles until dawn.
failure.art: A teenager and two small kids huddled in a pink bathtub piled with pillows, a shadowy hand pressed against a frosted bathroom window

encounters.title: The Last One Standing
encounters.place: Glimmer Falls High, after the lights go out
encounters.text: You only came back for your backpack. The hall lights die one bank at a time, and at the far end of the trophy hallway a figure in janitor's coveralls and a grinning homecoming-king mask lifts a pair of hedge trimmers. Snip. Snip. Every slasher movie you have rented says the same thing: run.
encounters.art: A long high school hallway in darkness, rows of lockers and a glass trophy case, a figure in gray janitor's coveralls and a grinning rubber homecoming-king mask with a plastic crown holding a pair of hedge trimmers low at the far end, a teenager with a backpack frozen in a pool of red emergency light in the foreground, deep shadow between them, long one-point view down the hall

choices.label: Sprint the long hallway for the gym doors

success.text: You hit the push bar at full speed and burst into the gym. You slap every light switch on the panel and yank the fire alarm. Lights blaze, bells scream, sprinklers rain. When you turn around, the doorway is empty except for a dropped pair of hedge trimmers.
success.art: A teenager bursting into a high-school gym under blazing lights and spraying sprinklers, a fire alarm handle pulled down, abandoned hedge trimmers on the threshold

failure.text: The hallway is longer than it should be. Lockers slam shut one after another behind you, getting closer. You dive into an open locker and pull it shut. The janitor finds you there at six in the morning and lets you out without a word.
failure.art: A teenager peering out through the slats of a high-school locker in a dark hallway, a long shadow with hedge trimmers passing outside

choices.label: Duck into the chem lab and improvise

success.text: Baking soda, vinegar, the dish soap from the sink, all in the big beaker. Foam floods the doorway just as the mask comes through. Its sneakers skid, it windmills, and it sails backward through the open window into the hedges. When you look out, the hedge is empty.
success.art: A wave of white foam spilling across a chemistry lab floor, a masked figure in coveralls slipping backward toward an open window, a teenager holding an empty beaker

failure.text: Everything you mix just goes puff in a little purple cloud. The masked figure walks calmly through the smoke, whistling, and you leave by the window yourself, landing in the rosebushes with half your jacket left behind on the latch.
failure.art: A masked figure strolling through a puff of purple smoke in a chemistry lab while a teenager scrambles out a window into rosebushes

choices.label: Grab the state championship trophy and stand your ground

success.text: You smash the trophy case, grab the 1979 softball state cup and swing. The mask cracks clean in half and falls off. There is nobody inside. The coveralls crumple to the floor like laundry, and the hedge trimmers clatter down beside them.
success.art: A teenager swinging a gold trophy cup at a masked figure, the mask splitting in half to reveal empty darkness, coveralls collapsing like laundry, glass from a trophy case glittering

failure.text: The trophy is plastic. It bounces off the mask with a hollow bonk, and the grin seems to get wider. You flee out the fire door with the alarm wailing and do not stop running until you reach the bike racks.
failure.art: A plastic trophy bouncing off a grinning homecoming-king mask, a teenager fleeing through a fire exit with an alarm light flashing red

encounters.title: Lookout Point
encounters.place: The lookout below the KGLM water tower
encounters.text: You and some friends are parked at the lookout in a borrowed car, watching the town lights and counting meteors. The radio cuts in with a bulletin about a man seen near the reservoir with a rusty garden hook. Then something on the roof of the car goes scrape. Scrape. Scrape.
encounters.art: A boxy 1980s sedan parked at a hilltop lookout at night above the glittering lights of a small town, three teens inside staring up at the car roof with wide eyes, the dashboard radio glowing, a meteor streaking across the starry sky, and a rusty garden hook glinting where it scrapes across the top of the windshield, starlight and green dash glow, medium wide shot

choices.label: Floor it down the switchbacks

success.text: Gravel sprays, everyone screams, then everyone laughs, and you fishtail all the way down Tower Road. At the bottom you get out to check the car. An old rusted garden hook is dangling from the door handle. You leave it in the ditch where it belongs.
success.art: Teens laughing in a car fishtailing down a winding hill road at night, a rusted garden hook swinging from the passenger door handle

failure.text: The engine floods and dies. The scraping slides from the roof to the trunk to the passenger door and back again, slow circles, until a pair of headlights comes up the hill and the sound stops all at once.
failure.art: A stalled car at a dark lookout, teens huddled inside, scratch marks spiraling around the car's paint, distant headlights climbing the hill

choices.label: Call the KGLM request line from the payphone and get on the air

success.text: Mix puts you on the air live. "Glimmer Falls, if you are up, flash your porch light for the kids at the lookout." Below, the whole town blinks on, hundreds of lights. Something heavy drops off your roof and crashes away into the pines, outnumbered.
success.art: A view from a hilltop lookout of an entire small town flashing its porch lights, a hulking shadow fleeing into the pine trees, a teen holding a payphone receiver

failure.text: The payphone line connects, but KGLM is only playing one sound: a slow scrape, scrape, scrape, in perfect time with the car roof. You hang up and sprint back to the car, and the scrape is still on the radio inside it.
failure.art: A teenager dropping a payphone receiver at a dark lookout, a car radio glowing behind them with sound lines in the shape of scratches

encounters.title: Last Pick of the Patch
encounters.place: Halvorsen's Pumpkin Patch, off Quarry Road, after closing
encounters.text: Every jack-o-lantern in the patch has lit itself. The scarecrow is missing from its post. From the corn maze comes the wet, patient scrape of someone carving, and then a figure steps out with a sack-cloth face, a pumpkin for a head, and a carving knife the size of a canoe paddle.
encounters.art: A moonlit pumpkin patch after closing time full of glowing jack-o'-lanterns that have lit themselves, an empty wooden scarecrow post, and a lanky figure with a burlap shirt and a carved pumpkin for a head stepping out of a dark corn maze holding a huge pumpkin-carving scoop the size of a shovel, a teenager crouched behind a hay bale, orange pumpkin glow and blue moonlight, wide shot

choices.label: Lose it in the corn maze

success.text: Left, left, right, double back. You hear it crash through a wall of corn and then a thump and a muffled oof as it runs straight into the hay-bale pyramid. You stroll out the exit. Behind you, a pumpkin head pokes up from the hay, looking embarrassed.
success.art: A teenager walking calmly out of a corn maze exit while behind them a pumpkin-headed figure sits buried to the neck in toppled hay bales

failure.text: The maze rearranges every time you turn a corner. Every path leads you back to the empty scarecrow post. On the fifth time, the post is not empty. It is wearing your jacket.
failure.art: A scarecrow post in a corn maze clearing wearing a teenager's jacket, the teenager stopped short in shock, corn walls leaning in

choices.label: Smash the brightest jack-o-lantern

success.text: You find the biggest, brightest, meanest-grinning pumpkin and give it a home-run swing. Every lantern in the patch goes out at once. In the dark, the pumpkin-head figure folds up like a dropped scarecrow, nothing but straw and a sack.
success.art: A teenager mid-swing smashing a giant glowing jack-o-lantern, every other lantern in the patch going dark, a scarecrow collapsing into straw behind them

failure.text: The pumpkin explodes into a geyser of seeds and orange goo that coats you from head to sneakers. Every other jack-o-lantern in the patch laughs, all at once, and the giant knife scrapes on a stone somewhere close behind you.
failure.art: A teenager drenched head to toe in orange pumpkin goo and seeds, surrounded by dozens of jack-o-lanterns with wide laughing faces

encounters.title: Lights Out at the Rink
encounters.place: The roller-rink annex at Pump Iron Gym, late skate
encounters.text: Halfway through the late skate the lights cut out, but the mirror ball keeps turning. When the emergency lights stutter on, there is one extra skater on the floor: a figure in a striped referee shirt and a yellow smiley-face mask, gliding backward, carrying a skate key the size of a crowbar.
encounters.art: A roller rink during a blackout lit only by a spinning mirror ball and red emergency lights, teens on skates scattering toward the walls, and one masked skater in a striped referee shirt and a yellow smiley-face mask gliding backward across the floor carrying a skate key the size of a crowbar, a teenager clinging to the rail, white sparkles and red glow, wide shot

choices.label: Outskate it around the rink

success.text: You grab hands with every skater you pass and form a crack-the-whip, faster and faster. At the end of the line you let go and go flying out the exit doors into the parking lot. The masked skater cannot make the turn and slams into the snack bar.
success.art: A line of teens on roller skates doing crack the whip around a rink, the last skater flying out through exit doors, a masked skater crashing into a snack bar counter

failure.text: You hit a dropped Bolt Cola can and go down hard, wheels spinning. The smiley face looms over you and taps the giant key on its palm. Then the DJ brings the lights up and it is gone, but your laces have been tied together.
failure.art: A teenager sprawled on a roller rink floor with skate wheels spinning, laces knotted together, a smiley-face mask fading into the mirror-ball sparkle above them

choices.label: Reach the DJ booth and kill the music

success.text: You lift the needle off the record. The masked skater freezes mid-glide, like it is playing musical statues and cannot help it. You leave it there, frozen in the mirror-ball light, and find a quarter on the floor of the booth on your way out.
success.art: A teenager lifting a needle off a spinning record in a DJ booth, a masked skater frozen mid-glide on the rink below, a quarter glinting on the booth floor

failure.text: The record changes by itself to a slow ballad. The speakers announce COUPLES ONLY. Every other skater pairs off and rolls away into the dark, leaving you alone on the floor with the smiley face and its outstretched hand.
failure.art: An empty roller rink under a mirror ball, a masked skater offering a gloved hand to a lone teenager, couples skating away into the shadows

encounters.title: Across the Street
encounters.place: Your bedroom window, after midnight
encounters.text: Someone in a pale, blank Halloween-store mask is standing under the streetlight by the roundabout, perfectly still, facing your house. You look away to grab your glasses. When you look back, it is one lawn closer. You look away again. Two lawns.
encounters.art: The view from a dark teenage bedroom window over a suburban cul-de-sac after midnight, a teenager's hand holding eyeglasses in the foreground, and on a neighbor's lawn under a streetlight a figure in a pale blank store-bought mask and a dark coverall standing perfectly still facing the house, one lawn closer to the window than the empty streetlight pool by the roundabout, cold white streetlight, wide shot over the shoulder

choices.label: Snap a picture to prove it's real

success.text: Flash. The instant photo develops slowly: the streetlight, the lawn, and in the figure's place, a garden gnome wearing a cheap rubber mask. When you look up, the lawn is empty. The gnome is back in the Fergusons' flowerbed, and the mask is in their trash can.
success.art: A developing instant photo showing a garden gnome wearing a rubber mask under a streetlight, a teenager's hand holding it by a bedroom window

failure.text: Flash. The instant photo develops slowly: your bedroom, your back, and the mask standing directly behind you. You spin around. Nobody. When you look out the window again, the streetlight is empty too.
failure.art: An instant photo showing a teenager at a window with a pale masked figure standing right behind them, the real bedroom behind the teen empty

choices.label: Wake the whole street with the phone tree

success.text: You call the Lindqvists, who call the Fergusons, who call everyone. Porch lights pop on all around the cul-de-sac. Neighbors step out in bathrobes with flashlights and garden rakes. The figure is gone. On the lawn where it stood is a dropped mask and a flattened circle of grass.
success.art: Neighbors in bathrobes stepping onto porches with flashlights and rakes all around a lit-up cul-de-sac, a dropped pale mask lying on an empty lawn

failure.text: Nobody picks up. Then your phone rings once. Then the house next door rings once, you can hear it through the wall. Then the next house closer, and the next, one ring per house, walking toward yours.
failure.art: A teenager clutching a phone in a dark kitchen while sound rings ripple from house to house down the street toward theirs

choices.label: Refuse to blink

success.text: You stare it down for twenty full minutes. Your eyes burn. Then, slowly, it takes a step backward. And another. Lawn by lawn, it retreats to the streetlight and out of the light and gone. You blink, finally, and laugh until you cry.
success.art: A teenager with wide, unblinking eyes pressed to a bedroom window while a masked figure retreats backward across lawns into the dark

failure.text: Your eyes water and close for half a heartbeat. When they open, the mask is pressed flat to your window glass, its breath fogging the pane. Then it is gone, and there is only a smudge on the outside of a second-story window.
failure.art: A blank pale mask pressed against a second-story bedroom window from outside, breath fog on the glass, a teenager recoiling

encounters.title: Full Service
encounters.place: Sudsy's Auto Wash on Main Street, after closing
encounters.text: You cut through Sudsy's Auto Wash on your bike because it is shorter. The machinery grinds awake behind you. Blue foam gushes from the nozzles, the giant brushes start to spin, and deep inside the tunnel a figure in a yellow rain slicker and a grinning cartoon-frog mask is waiting, holding a squeegee on a ten-foot pole.
encounters.art: A dark automatic car wash tunnel at night, the giant blue brushes spinning and blue foam gushing from the nozzles, a figure in a yellow rain slicker and a grinning cartoon-frog mask standing deep inside the tunnel holding a squeegee on a ten-foot pole, a teenager on a bicycle stopped at the entrance with one foot down, wet concrete and blue tunnel light, wide shot

choices.label: Ride your bike straight through on the conveyor track

success.text: You hit the track at full speed. Brushes slap left and right, the rinse blasts you, and the frog mask lunges just as the hot-air blower kicks on and launches it backward into the foam. You shoot out the far end, shining and grinning. Lou, waiting by the vacuums, holds up ten fingers: a perfect score.
success.art: A teenager on a bike bursting out of the exit of a car wash tunnel in a spray of foam and hot air, a frog-masked figure in a yellow slicker tumbling backward into the suds behind them
success.alone: You hit the track at full speed. Brushes slap left and right, the rinse blasts you, and the frog mask lunges just as the hot-air blower kicks on and launches it backward into the foam. You shoot out the far end, shining and grinning, and take a victory lap around the vacuum stalls.

failure.text: The conveyor grabs your back wheel and drags you in slow motion through the whole wash: pre-soak, brushes, hot wax, rinse. The frog mask strolls alongside the entire way, squeegeeing your face. You come out the other end soaked to the bone and smelling like cherry air freshener.
failure.art: A dripping teenager on a bike being pulled slowly through a car wash on a conveyor, a frog-masked figure in a yellow slicker walking beside them squeegeeing their face

choices.label: Find the control box and shut the whole wash down

success.text: The control box is behind the change machine. You pull the big red lever. The brushes droop, the foam slumps, and in the sudden quiet the frog mask slips on the wet floor and slides, very slowly, the whole length of the tunnel into a drain grate, stuck at the waist. On your way out you scoop up the quarters spilled from the change machine.
success.art: A frog-masked figure in a yellow slicker stuck waist-deep in a drain grate in a silent car wash tunnel, drooping brushes, a teenager pocketing coins beside a change machine

failure.text: You pull the wrong lever and the wash jumps to DELUXE. Hot wax sprays from every nozzle, the brushes spin double time, and the frog mask waves at you through the foam. You escape over the back fence with your hair waxed into a rock-hard pompadour that will take three shampoos to undo.
failure.art: A teenager scrambling over a chain-link fence behind a car wash spraying foam and hot wax, their hair waxed into a towering shiny pompadour, a frog mask waving from the suds

choices.label: Dive into the foam pile and hold your breath

success.text: You sink into a mountain of blue bubbles and go perfectly still. Rubber boots squeak past an inch from your nose. The slicker pauses, sniffs, and moves on into the rinse cycle, where the giant blowers sweep it right out the back of the building and into the dumpster with a clang.
success.art: A teenager's eyes peeking out of a mountain of blue foam in a car wash, rubber boots squeaking past, a yellow-slickered figure being blown out the back by giant air dryers

failure.text: The foam is warm and quiet, and then it starts to drain. It sinks lower and lower until you are sitting in plain sight on the wet concrete, and the frog mask is crouched right in front of you, head tilted. You bolt out the back into the dark and keep running into whatever is waiting there.
failure.art: A teenager crouched on wet concrete as the last of the foam drains away around them, a frog-masked figure in a yellow slicker crouched face to face with them, head tilted

encounters.title: Which One Moved?
encounters.place: The dead wing of the Starlight Mall, after closing
encounters.text: The dead wing of Starlight Mall is a row of stores that closed years ago, and every display window is still crowded with mannequins in dusty 1970s fashions. You pass the old Glamarama Boutique. There were six mannequins in that window. Now there are seven, and the seventh has a blank white face, a security guard's cap and a pricing gun that goes click, click, click.
encounters.art: A dim abandoned mall corridor after closing, a dusty boutique display window crowded with mannequins in 1970s flared pants and wide-collared shirts, and among them one extra blank white-faced figure in a security guard's cap holding a pricing gun, a teenager walking past with their reflection in the glass, a flashlight beam on the window, gray dust and cold light, medium shot

choices.label: Hop into the next window and pose like a mannequin

success.text: You hop into the window of the old shoe store and strike a pose. The figure walks the length of the wing, studying every dummy, clicking price tags onto their sleeves. It reaches you, stares, clicks a tag onto your jacket that says CLEARANCE, and moves on. You stay frozen until its footsteps fade, then peel off the tag and run.
success.art: A teenager frozen in a stiff pose among dusty mannequins in a shoe store window, a blank-faced figure in a guard cap sticking a price tag on their sleeve

failure.text: Your nose itches. You hold it for three whole minutes, and then you sneeze. Every mannequin in the dead wing turns its head toward you at once, with a sound like knuckles cracking. You run, and they clatter after you as far as the food court before collapsing into a heap of plastic arms.
failure.art: Dozens of mannequins in a dark mall corridor all turning their heads toward a sneezing teenager at once, plastic arms reaching out from every display window

choices.label: Shoulder through the display door like a lineman

success.text: Moose lowers his shoulder beside you, and on three you hit the display like the varsity front line. Mannequins topple like bowling pins. Under the pile, the figure is just one more plastic dummy with a cap on its head and a pricing gun glued to its hand. Moose stands it back up, apologetically, and you walk out laughing.
success.art: Mannequins toppling like bowling pins in a dusty boutique window, a teenager mid-tackle, a plastic dummy in a guard cap lying on top of the pile with a pricing gun glued to its hand
success.alone: You lower your shoulder and hit the display like the varsity front line. Mannequins topple like bowling pins. Under the pile, the figure is just one more plastic dummy with a cap on its head and a pricing gun glued to its hand. You stand it back up, apologetically, and walk out laughing.

failure.text: You hit the pile and the mannequins hug you back. Plastic arms lock around your middle, your shoulders, your knees, and for one awful moment you are part of the display. You wriggle free, leaving your jacket on a dummy in a leisure suit and a tag stuck to your forehead that reads SOLD.
failure.art: A teenager tangled in the plastic arms of a crowd of mannequins in a boutique window, a price tag stuck to their forehead, one mannequin in a leisure suit wearing their jacket

choices.label: Sweep a light across their faces and watch the shadows

success.text: Mannequins do not flinch. You sweep your beam down the row, one, two, three, and on the seventh the shadow jumps before the figure does. "Gotcha," you say. It drops the pricing gun and bolts for the fire exit, setting off the alarm, and the mall lights blaze on all the way down the wing.
success.art: A flashlight beam sweeping across a row of mannequins in a mall window, one blank-faced figure in a guard cap flinching from the light, its shadow jumping on the wall

failure.text: Every shadow flinches. All of them. You back away down the corridor, and seven shadows peel off the wall and follow, sliding along the dead storefronts beside you, all the way to the exit doors, and out into the night with you.
failure.art: Seven dark shadows peeling off a wall and sliding along empty mall storefronts beside a teenager backing toward the exit doors with a flashlight

encounters.title: Last Call, Kiddo
encounters.place: Crystal Street and every street after it, a quarter to one
encounters.text: An ice cream truck is crawling down Crystal Street at a quarter to one in the morning, its music-box jingle slowed to a dirge. The serving window slides open. The driver wears a paper hat and a giant grinning ice-cream-cone mask, and he holds up a scoop the size of a garden shovel. "Last call, kiddo," he says, and the truck turns to follow you.
encounters.art: A boxy white ice cream truck creeping down a dark suburban cul-de-sac at a quarter to one in the morning, its painted side of cones and popsicles glowing, a driver in a paper hat and a giant grinning ice-cream-cone mask leaning out the serving window holding a scoop the size of a garden shovel, a teenager on a bicycle caught in the truck's headlights, pastel truck lights and blue night, wide shot

choices.label: Race it through the backyards

success.text: You cut through the Delgados' side yard, hop the Lindqvists' sprinkler line and fly down the drainage ditch where no truck can follow. Sunny rolls up alongside you in her racing chair, whooping, and the two of you coast to a stop at the end of the ditch as the dirge fades into the distance.
success.art: A teenager on a bike and a wheelchair racer flying side by side down a moonlit concrete drainage ditch, an ice cream truck's headlights stuck at the top of the bank behind them
success.alone: You cut through the Delgados' side yard, hop the Lindqvists' sprinkler line and fly down the drainage ditch where no truck can follow. You coast to a stop at the end of it, lungs burning and grinning, as the dirge fades into the distance.

failure.text: Every shortcut you take, the truck is already idling at the end of it, music playing, scoop raised. In the fourth backyard your chain pops off. You hide in a doghouse with a very confused beagle until the dirge finally drifts away, a little before dawn.
failure.art: A teenager squeezed into a backyard doghouse beside a confused beagle, a dropped bike with a loose chain on the lawn, an ice cream truck's glowing menu board visible over the fence

choices.label: Walk right up and order a double with sprinkles

success.text: You stroll up to the window and order a double with sprinkles, extra polite. The mask tilts, as if you are the first customer in years. It scoops slowly and carefully and hands it over, the music box speeds back up to its happy tempo, and the truck drives off with its lights blinking like a wave. It even gives you change from a dollar you never handed over.
success.art: A teenager at the window of an ice cream truck on a dark street receiving a tall cone with sprinkles from a driver in a grinning ice-cream-cone mask, the truck's lights blinking cheerfully

failure.text: You order a double with sprinkles. The mask tilts, then leans all the way out the window, and the scoop comes down on your head like a cap: one huge, cold dollop of rocky road. "On the house," it says. The truck idles behind you all the way home, playing the jingle slower and slower.
failure.art: A teenager with a huge scoop of rocky road ice cream on top of their head walking home down a dark street, an ice cream truck idling close behind with its grinning cone-masked driver

choices.label: Tape the jingle and play it back at the wrong speed

success.text: You record ten seconds of the dirge and play it back on fast-forward, a chipmunk squeal of a jingle. The truck lurches, the music box hiccups into the same squeaky tempo, and the driver clutches his mask with both hands and roars away down Quarry Road like a dog hearing a whistle.
success.art: A teenager holding up a portable cassette recorder on a dark street, an ice cream truck swerving away in a cloud of exhaust, its cone-masked driver clutching his head with both hands

failure.text: You play the tape back and it is not the jingle. It is your own voice, recorded somewhere you have never been, saying "Last call, kiddo." The truck honks its horn in delight. You fling the recorder into a hedge, run, and have to dig it out of the boxwood at dawn.
failure.art: A teenager staring in horror at a portable cassette recorder in their hand on a dark street, an ice cream truck honking behind them, its cone-masked driver laughing

encounters.title: The Gopher Under the Bleachers
encounters.place: Under the football bleachers at Glimmer Falls High, late
encounters.text: You are crawling around under the bleachers hunting for the retainer you lost at practice. Up in the seats, something is coming down: thump, thump, thump, one row at a time. The scoreboard flickers on by itself and reads HOME 0, GUEST 1. Then Goldie the Gopher, the Little League mascot, drops down beside you with huge foam buck teeth and a megaphone it never says a word through.
encounters.art: The dark underside of high school football bleachers at night, stripes of stadium light falling through the slats, a teenager on hands and knees searching the gravel with a flashlight, and crouched between the steel struts beside them a giant foam gopher mascot with huge buck teeth and a megaphone, a lit scoreboard glowing beyond the bleachers, medium shot

choices.label: Belt out the school fight song with all the arm motions

success.text: Chip knows every verse from three years of pep rallies, and he takes the harmony while you take the arm motions. The gopher freezes. Its foam head bobs, its big foot taps, and then it is doing the routine with you, cartwheel and all. When you finish it bows deeply and waddles off toward the locker room. The scoreboard flips to HOME 1.
success.art: A teenager doing a cheer routine with a giant foam gopher mascot mid-cartwheel on a moonlit football field, a lit scoreboard behind them
success.alone: You belt out every off-key verse, arm motions and all. The gopher freezes. Its foam head bobs, its big foot taps, and then it is doing the routine with you, cartwheel and all. When you finish it bows deeply and waddles off toward the locker room. The scoreboard flips to HOME 1.

failure.text: You hit the first note and the megaphone finally rises. It does not shout. It plays your own voice back, the high, cracking part, over the stadium speakers, on a loop, to an empty field. The gopher's foam shoulders shake with silent laughter as you sprint for the parking lot.
failure.art: A teenager sprinting across a dark football field toward the parking lot, a giant foam gopher mascot holding up a megaphone, stadium speakers glowing on their poles

choices.label: Tackle it and pop off the giant head

success.text: You hit it at the knees, textbook, and the giant head pops off and rolls across the turf. The costume is stuffed with old pep-rally streamers and about a hundred lost retainers, yours sitting right on top. The body slumps like a beanbag. You take your retainer and the loose change rattling around in the costume's pouch.
success.art: A giant foam gopher mascot head rolling across a moonlit football field, the slumped costume spilling paper streamers, a triumphant teenager holding up a retainer

failure.text: You tackle it and bounce off the foam like a trampoline. The head stays on. The gopher picks you up by the back of your jacket, very gently, carries you to the fifty-yard line and sets you down facing the end zone just as the sprinklers come on. You run the length of the field through every one of them.
failure.art: A giant foam gopher mascot carrying a teenager by the back of their jacket onto a dark football field as every sprinkler bursts on in arcs of water

choices.label: Belly-crawl out the far end of the bleachers

success.text: You belly-crawl through popcorn boxes and gum wrappers to the far end, where the fence has a gap only freshmen know about. The thumping stops behind you, confused. From the parking lot you watch the gopher standing alone on the field, scratching its enormous foam head.
success.art: A giant foam gopher mascot standing alone on a moonlit football field scratching its head, a teenager peeking back through a gap in a chain-link fence

failure.text: You crawl, and something crawls beside you, matching your pace on the other side of a row of struts. When you stop, it stops. At the fence gap a giant foam paw is already waiting, holding it open for you, politely. You squeeze through and do not stop running until you are home.
failure.art: A teenager crawling under dark bleachers, a giant foam gopher paw holding open a gap in a chain-link fence ahead of them, two glinting button eyes between the struts

name: Creature Feature
blurb: Something slithered up from the storm drains, something hatched in the pet shop, and the hedge animals in the roundabout have started to wander. In Glimmer Falls, nature is fighting back, and it brought teeth.

encounters.title: Something in the Storm Drains
encounters.place: The storm grate at the end of Crystal Street
encounters.text: It rained all evening, and now the storm grate at the end of the street is making a sound like a giant slurping the last of a milkshake. Two round lights, the color of taillights, blink at you from down in the dark. A kid's lost sneaker on the curb slides, by itself, toward the grate and drops in.
encounters.art: A rain-slick suburban curb at night after an evening of rain, an iron storm drain grate with two round glowing red eyes blinking in the darkness below it, a child's lost sneaker sliding along the wet gutter toward the grate by itself, a teenager in a raincoat crouched a few steps back, orange streetlight reflected in the puddles, low medium shot

choices.label: Lower a flashlight on a jump rope and look

success.text: The beam finds a white alligator the size of a canoe, wearing a faded Pet Paradise collar from 1979. It is not angry. It is lonely and hungry. You drop it a package of bologna. It blinks slowly, the way cats do when they like you, and slides away down the tunnel.
success.art: A flashlight beam on a jump rope lighting a huge pale alligator in a storm drain tunnel, a faded pet-shop collar around its neck, a slice of bologna falling toward its open jaws

failure.text: The rope goes taut, then yanks out of your hands. Your flashlight beam tumbles down, down, down, and then goes crunch. From the grate comes a long, satisfied burp that rattles every garbage can on the street.
failure.art: A jump rope whipping down into a storm drain, a flashlight beam tumbling into darkness, garbage cans rattling along the curb

choices.label: Pry up the grate and climb down after the sneaker

success.text: Knee-deep in cold water, you find a nest: lost sneakers, tennis balls, three flying discs and a pile of coins, all arranged with care. It has been collecting. Something huge rumbles behind you like an outboard motor purring. You leave it a flying disc and keep the change it offers.
success.art: A teenager knee-deep in a storm drain tunnel beside a nest of lost sneakers, tennis balls, flying discs and coins, a huge shadowy reptile curled contentedly behind them

failure.text: The current knocks you flat and carries you through a mile of tunnels. You get spat out of a drain in the Starlight Mall parking lot at four in the morning, smelling exactly like the food court dumpsters.
failure.art: A soaked teenager crawling out of a storm drain in an empty mall parking lot at night, neon mall signs dark, a puddle of greasy water around them

encounters.title: Pets After Dark
encounters.place: Pet Paradise, lower level of the Starlight Mall, after closing
encounters.text: On a dare, you hid in the photo booth until the mall closed. Now every cage in Pet Paradise is open. The hamster wheels spin in the dark. The parakeets are whispering your name, all together. And in the aquarium aisle, something big and shaggy is eating the fish food straight out of the tubs.
encounters.art: A dark mall pet shop after closing lit only by glowing blue aquarium tanks, every cage door hanging open, hamster wheels spinning in the dark, a row of parakeets lined up on a shelf all turned toward a teenager peeking out from behind a counter, and in the aquarium aisle a huge shaggy silhouette hunched over open tubs of fish food, blue water light, wide shot

choices.label: Herd everything back into its cage

success.text: You make soft clicking sounds and the puppies follow you like a parade. The snake coils back into its tank, the parakeets hop onto their perch. The big shaggy thing turns out to be a tortoise the size of a coffee table, wearing a toupee of moss. It lets you scratch its chin.
success.art: A teenager leading a parade of puppies back to their pens in a moonlit pet shop, a coffee-table-sized tortoise with a mossy shell stretching its chin to be scratched

failure.text: The parakeets learn your name perfectly and scream it at the top of their lungs. Mall security's flashlight swings toward the shop. You hide under the fish tanks for an hour while forty birds tell the guard exactly where you are.
failure.art: A teenager hiding under a row of glowing fish tanks while a mall security guard's flashlight sweeps the store, parakeets shrieking on every perch

choices.label: Follow the crumbs to the big one

success.text: It is a guinea pig. It is a guinea pig the size of a Saint Bernard, and it is very sorry about the fish food. It squeaks, a sound like a tea kettle. You scratch behind its enormous ears, and it nudges open the service door so you can get out of the mall.
success.art: A teenager scratching the ears of an enormous fluffy guinea pig the size of a large dog in a pet-shop aisle, a service door propped open behind them

failure.text: The crumbs lead in a circle. You realize it is behind you a second before it sneezes. You are coated, head to toe, in something warm and green. You run for the dead wing and do not look back.
failure.art: A teenager drenched in green slime running through a dark mall corridor, a giant shaggy shape sniffling in a pet-shop doorway behind them

encounters.title: The Roundabout Hedges
encounters.place: The roundabout garden, Crystal Street
encounters.text: The topiary animals in the roundabout garden have moved. The hedge swan is standing in the street. The hedge poodle is on the Kowalskis' lawn, digging. The hedge rabbit is gone completely, and from the dark between the houses comes the sound of leaves rustling against siding, getting closer.
encounters.art: A suburban roundabout garden at night with empty topiary plinths, a clipped green hedge swan standing in the middle of the street, a hedge poodle digging up a neighbor's lawn with soil flying, a teenager in a sweatshirt backing away on the sidewalk, and in the dark gap between two houses a tall leafy shape rustling against the siding, streetlight and blue moonlight, wide shot

choices.label: Borrow the Lindqvists' hedge clippers

success.text: Snip, snip, snip. The poodle sheds its pompoms and sits, ashamed, on the lawn. The swan honks and waddles home. The rabbit comes hopping out from behind a garage and climbs back onto its plinth on its own. By sunrise, the garden looks freshly trimmed.
success.art: A teenager with long hedge clippers trimming a topiary poodle on a lawn at night, a topiary swan waddling back toward the roundabout, a hedge rabbit climbing onto its plinth

failure.text: The privet grabs the clippers, then your sleeve, then the rest of you. You spend the night stuck in the hedge poodle like a burr, until the automatic sprinklers come on at five and it lets you go, sputtering.
failure.art: A teenager tangled inside a topiary poodle on a dark lawn, only their sneakers and one arm sticking out, sprinklers spraying at dawn

choices.label: Turn on every sprinkler on the street

success.text: You know where every spigot on the route is. One by one the lawns hiss to life. The topiaries sigh, drink, and stroll back to the roundabout like cats after dinner, settling on their plinths with their leaves glistening. The swan even fluffs itself.
success.art: Sprinklers spraying across moonlit lawns, topiary animals walking contentedly back to their plinths in a roundabout garden, leaves sparkling with water

failure.text: The water makes them grow. In minutes, the hedge swan is two stories tall and peering in your bedroom window with a leafy, curious eye. It is still there when you wake up, and the Lindqvists are going to need a ladder.
failure.art: A giant two-story topiary swan peering into a teenager's upstairs bedroom window at dawn, sprinklers still running on the lawn below

encounters.title: Something Got Out of the Clinic
encounters.place: The garage veterinary clinic, Crystal Street
encounters.text: The side door of the garage clinic is swinging open. Inside, a crate rattles on the floor, its tag reading DO NOT FEED AFTER DARK in marker. The crate is empty. From the rafters, between the Christmas decorations and the camping gear, something hisses and blinks three eyes at you.
encounters.art: A suburban garage converted into a veterinary clinic at night, its side door swinging open, an empty pet crate with a paper tag on its handle lying on the concrete with its gate bent outward, and up in the rafters between boxes of Christmas decorations and camping gear three glowing yellow eyes blinking down, a teenager in the doorway with a flashlight, single hanging work light, medium shot

choices.label: Coax it down with a can of tuna

success.text: It is an opossum with three eyes and a soft purple glow in its belly, and it loves tuna. It climbs down your arm, purrs like a cat, and curls up back in its crate. In the morning there is a thank-you note on your door: It likes you. Most people it bites. A.H.
success.art: A three-eyed opossum with a softly glowing purple belly eating tuna from a can in a teenager's hands in a dim garage clinic

failure.text: It drops onto your head and settles in like a hat. It refuses to leave. You run in circles in the driveway, waking every dog on the street, while it chirps happily and steers you by the ears.
failure.art: A teenager running in circles on a driveway at night with a three-eyed opossum perched on their head like a hat, porch lights flicking on

choices.label: Throw a tarp over it and grab

success.text: One throw and the tarp comes down over the whole lump. It wiggles, chirps, and gives up. You slide it back into its crate and latch it. The next day there are two quarters in your mailbox with a sketch of a three-eyed smiley face.
success.art: A teenager wrestling a wiggling tarp-covered lump into a pet crate in a garage, a stern warning tag tied to the crate

failure.text: The lump under the tarp splits into four smaller lumps, and all four scatter in different directions across Crystal Street. You hear them chirping in the hedges for the rest of the night, and one of them seems to be in your attic.
failure.art: Four small lumps scurrying out from under a tarp in different directions across a dark cul-de-sac, a teenager staring in dismay

encounters.title: The Glimmer Falls Grabber
